title: News Gapper
teaches: The News Gapper as we trade it: a fresh named catalyst, most often an earnings report, gaps a liquid stock up on at least three times its average volume; the gap holds and the day closes green in the upper half; the buy is the first pullback and reclaim, a market order as price trades over the prior day's high after two down days or an inside day that hold the gap-day low, or day one over the opening-range high for an A+; the stop sits a few cents under the pullback low, a third comes off at 3R and 5R with the rest on the 10-day or 21-day trail, and a loss taken at the stop is the system working.

questions.q: In one line, what is a News Gapper?
choices: A catalyst gap that holds its range
A gap on rumors that fills by lunch
A gap with no named news behind it
A slow drift over several weeks
questions.answer: A catalyst gap that holds its range
questions.why: A catalyst gap that holds its range. A fresh, named catalyst gaps a liquid stock up, and the day holds the gap instead of giving it back.
questions.lesson_line: A News Gapper is a named catalyst gap that holds.

wrong.A gap on rumors that fills by lunch: A gap that fills is the opposite: that is a failed gap.
wrong.A gap with no named news behind it: Without a catalyst there is no News Gapper.
wrong.A slow drift over several weeks: A News Gapper is a gap day, not a drift.

questions.q: A News Gapper needs a fresh, named catalyst; a big gap on no news is not one.
questions.answer: True
questions.why: True. The catalyst is fresh and named, most often a report. Buying a gap with no catalyst, or a weak one, is a mistake.
questions.lesson_line: No named catalyst, no News Gapper.

questions.q: What must the gap day do for the gap to count as holding?
choices: Hold the gap, close in upper half
Close at the exact high of the day
Trade back to the prior close first
Close below the open
questions.answer: Hold the gap, close in upper half
questions.why: Stay above the prior close and close in the upper half of its range. The day never trades back to the prior close and closes green.
questions.lesson_line: A held gap never revisits the prior close.

wrong.Close at the exact high of the day: The close does not have to be the exact high; the upper half is the test.
wrong.Trade back to the prior close first: A trade back to the prior close means the gap filled.
wrong.Close below the open: A close below the open is a faded day.

Any; headlines ignore the market
questions.answer: Green or Yellow
questions.why: Green or Yellow. Orange allows A+ setups only, and Red is mostly cash and shorts.
questions.lesson_line: Read the market first: Green or Yellow for gappers.

wrong.Orange or Red: Orange is for A+ setups only, and Red is mostly cash.
wrong.Red only: Red means mostly cash and shorts, not new longs.
wrong.Any; headlines ignore the market: A good headline does not switch the market reading off.

questions.q: News and earnings gaps cluster in a few weeks of each earnings season.
questions.answer: True
questions.why: True. The gaps cluster in 3 to 4 weeks of earnings season each quarter, so those are the weeks to watch.
questions.lesson_line: Gaps cluster in earnings season. Watch those weeks.

questions.q: How much volume does a News Gapper need by the close?
choices: At least 3 times the 50-day average
Any volume if the gap is big
Just above the 50-day average
Less than the 50-day average
questions.answer: At least 3 times the 50-day average
questions.why: At least 3 times the 50-day average, and on pace for it by the opening-range buy. Kullamagi: volume is the number one thing to focus on.
questions.lesson_line: Three times average volume is the line.

wrong.Any volume if the gap is big: A big gap on thin volume is the trap; volume is the line.
wrong.Just above the 50-day average: Just above average is the B- zone, below the line.
wrong.Less than the 50-day average: Below average volume is the opposite of a news gap.

questions.q: The pullback buy waits for two down days or an inside day whose closes all hold the gap-day low.
questions.answer: True
questions.why: True. After two down days or an inside day that keep every close above the gap-day low, the buy is a market order over the prior day's high.
questions.lesson_line: The pullback must hold the gap-day low on every close.

questions.q: In the first ten sessions, which event ends the setup?
choices: A close under the gap-day low
An inside day
Two down days that hold the low
A quiet day on lighter volume
questions.answer: A close under the gap-day low
questions.why: A close under the gap-day low. The gap fills or the stock closes under the gap-day low in the first ten sessions.
questions.lesson_line: A close under the gap-day low ends it.

wrong.An inside day: An inside day is a pullback pattern we want.
wrong.Two down days that hold the low: Two down days that hold the gap-day low are the pullback itself.
wrong.A quiet day on lighter volume: A quiet day on lighter volume is part of a healthy pullback.

questions.q: A gap on good news that closes red is a News Failure, not a News Gapper.
questions.answer: True
questions.why: True. A red close after good news is the News Failure. Same headline, opposite trade.
questions.lesson_line: Same headline, red close: a different trade.

questions.q: Which headline is the strongest catalyst?
choices: A beat with a raised outlook
A mention on a morning TV show
One analyst upgrade to a buy
A vague press release about plans
questions.answer: A beat with a raised outlook
questions.why: An earnings beat with a raised outlook. Bonde: earnings, new products and raised guidance have a high probability of a multi-month rally. Mentions and upgrades do not.
questions.lesson_line: Earnings with a raise beats a mention or an upgrade.

wrong.A mention on a morning TV show: A media mention has a low probability of follow-through.
wrong.One analyst upgrade to a buy: An upgrade alone is a B- catalyst.
wrong.A vague press release about plans: A vague press release is a B- catalyst.

questions.q: When do we skip a news gapper's pullback buy?
choices: A report is due within 3 sessions
The stock is up on the day
Volume is above average
The market is Green
questions.answer: A report is due within 3 sessions
questions.why: A report is due within 3 sessions. We take no new buys in the 3 days before an earnings report.
questions.lesson_line: No new buys in the 3 days before a report.

wrong.The stock is up on the day: Being up on the day is how a reclaim looks.
wrong.Volume is above average: Above-average volume is a plus for a gapper.
wrong.The market is Green: Green is the reading we want.

questions.q: For an earnings gap, the fundamentals decide the grade before the chart is looked at.
questions.answer: False
questions.why: False. Growing sales and earnings, ideally accelerating, with a beat and raised guidance, are a grade cue. The chart comes first.
questions.lesson_line: Fundamentals are a cue. The chart decides.

questions.q: On a news gapper you may add shares when volume surges after the buy.
questions.answer: False
questions.why: False. The full size goes in at one price with one stop. No adding.
questions.lesson_line: One buy, one price, one stop.

questions.q: Bought at 105.11 with the stop at 103.20. Where is 3R?
questions.why: 110.84. One R is the fill minus the stop. Add three of those to the fill. TGT ran to 12.0R from these levels.
questions.lesson_line: Know your 3R before the open. The first third comes off there.

questions.q: Gap day: low 100.00, high 110.00, close 107.00. Where in the range did it close, from 0 to 1?
questions.why: 0.7. The close minus the low, divided by the high minus the low. That is the upper half of the range, so the gap holds.
questions.lesson_line: Close minus low, over the range. Upper half holds the gap.

questions.q: Where does the stop go on the pullback buy?
choices: A few cents under the pullback low
Under the gap-day low, however far
At the prior close, the gap-fill price
1% under the pullback low for room
questions.answer: A few cents under the pullback low
questions.why: A few cents under the pullback low. The gap-day low is the line that must hold, not the stop.
questions.lesson_line: The stop sits under the pullback low.

wrong.Under the gap-day low, however far: The gap-day low is the line that must hold, not the stop.
wrong.At the prior close, the gap-fill price: The prior close is the gap fill; a stop there is far too wide.
wrong.1% under the pullback low for room: No porosity: the stop is a few cents under, not a cushion.

questions.q: The last third trails a close under the 21-day for a fast mover or the 10-day for a steadier one.
questions.answer: False
questions.why: False. It is the other way round. Sell on a close under the 10-day for a fast mover or the 21-day for a steadier one.
questions.lesson_line: Trail the last third under the 10- or 21-day.

questions.q: Tap the number that fits the blank.
questions.sentence: After the third at 3R, another third comes off at ___R.
questions.why: 5. After the first third at 3R, another third comes off at 5R, then the last third trails.
questions.lesson_line: A third at 3R, a third at 5R.

questions.q: Which gap is an A+ gap?
choices: 10% or more, and a true gap
Any gap that fills partly by noon
A gap on average daily volume
A gap that closes red
questions.answer: 10% or more, and a true gap
questions.why: 10% or more, and a true gap. The day's low stays above the prior day's high.
questions.lesson_line: A+ gap: ten percent or more, and a true gap.

wrong.Any gap that fills partly by noon: A gap that fills is not holding.
wrong.A gap on average daily volume: Average volume is not the A+ cue.
wrong.A gap that closes red: A red close is a News Failure.

questions.q: A true gap means the day's low stays above the prior day's high.
questions.answer: True
questions.why: True. For an up gap, the low must be higher than the previous day's high.
questions.lesson_line: A true gap leaves a hole above yesterday's high.

questions.q: The 50-day average volume is 4 million shares. The gap day trades 13 million. What is the multiple?
questions.why: 3.25. Gap-day volume divided by the 50-day average. That clears the line of at least 3 times.
questions.lesson_line: Volume multiple is today over the 50-day average.

questions.q: What do you do?
questions.story: A stock gapped 12% on a contract headline and closed strong. Two down days followed, both closing above the gap-day low. This morning it trades over yesterday's high.
choices: Buy at market; stop under pullback low
Pass; day one was the only entry
Wait for the next report
Buy at the gap-day low with a limit
questions.answer: Buy at market; stop under pullback low
questions.why: Buy at market. After two down days that hold the gap-day low, the trigger is a market buy over the prior day's high. The stop goes a few cents under the pullback low.
questions.lesson_line: Buy as price trades over the prior day's high.

wrong.Pass; day one was the only entry: The pullback buy is the entry here; day one is not the only one.
wrong.Wait for the next report: Waiting for a report adds risk and drops the trigger.
wrong.Buy at the gap-day low with a limit: A limit down at the gap-day low misses the trigger and the line.

questions.q: Is there a buy?
questions.story: The pullback closes under the gap-day low on day 3. On day 4 the stock rallies and trades over the prior day's high.
choices: No; the gap-day low broke first
Yes; the reclaim is the trigger
Yes, at half size
Yes, with a stop at the gap fill
questions.answer: No; the gap-day low broke first
questions.why: No. The pullback broke the gap-day low on a close before any reclaim, so there is no Buy 2.
questions.lesson_line: A pullback that breaks the gap-day low has no buy.

wrong.Yes; the reclaim is the trigger: The reclaim only counts if the pullback held the gap-day low.
wrong.Yes, at half size: Half size on a broken setup is still a broken setup.
wrong.Yes, with a stop at the gap fill: A stop at the gap fill is far wider than the rules allow.

questions.q: Buy or pass?
questions.story: The reclaim level is 40.00. You were away from your desk, and at 10:30 the stock trades 41.80.
choices: Pass, over 4% above the trigger
Buy, the reclaim is confirmed
Buy half size to cut the risk
Buy with a wider stop to fit it
questions.answer: Pass, over 4% above the trigger
questions.why: Pass. 41.80 is more than 4% over the 40.00 reclaim level. Chasing costs size, not risk: the stop stays put and the shares shrink.
questions.lesson_line: Miss it rather than chase it. Four percent and done.

wrong.Buy, the reclaim is confirmed: Confirmed and too far away are both true. The chase line is 4%.
wrong.Buy half size to cut the risk: Half of a bad entry is still a bad entry.
wrong.Buy with a wider stop to fit it: A wider stop to fit a late entry is the mistake, not the fix.

questions.q: What do you do?
questions.story: A contract headline hits at 7:30 am. The stock is up 11% pre-market on big volume.
choices: Wait for the opening range, then decide
Buy now with a market order
Buy half now, half at the open
Place a stop-limit just under the gap
questions.answer: Wait for the opening range, then decide
questions.why: Wait. We never buy before the open. The opening range forms first, and the day-one buy, if any, comes over its high in regular hours.
questions.lesson_line: No pre-market buys. Let the opening range form.

wrong.Buy now with a market order: Entries are market orders in regular hours, not pre-market.
wrong.Buy half now, half at the open: Half a pre-market buy is still a pre-market buy.
wrong.Place a stop-limit just under the gap: A stop-limit under the gap is not an entry plan.

questions.q: What do you do?
questions.story: Your news gapper is up 7R after four straight up days. Two of them were gap ups, and each day's range was wider than the last.
choices: Sell a big part into it
Hold; the trail is the only exit
Add; momentum is strongest here
Sell everything at the open tomorrow
questions.answer: Sell a big part into it
questions.why: Sell a big part into it. Three to five straight up days with gaps and range expansion is a climax run, and you sell a big part.
questions.lesson_line: A climax run is the time to sell a big part.

wrong.Hold; the trail is the only exit: A climax run is a judgment call to sell a big part.
wrong.Add; momentum is strongest here: Adding to a climax run is how gains are given back.
wrong.Sell everything at the open tomorrow: Selling everything at once is not the plan; sell a big part.

questions.q: What do you do with the second third?
questions.story: You bought at 50.00 with the stop at 48.00, so 3R is 56.00 and 5R is 60.00. After the first third at 3R, the stock opens at 60.80.
choices: Sell it at the open, 60.80
Sell it at 60.00 with a limit
Hold it to the close
Hold it to 10R
questions.answer: Sell it at the open, 60.80
questions.why: Sell it at the open. If the stock gaps past a trim level, we trim at the open. Gappers often gap again.
questions.lesson_line: Opened past a trim level: take it at the open.

wrong.Sell it at 60.00 with a limit: The stock is already past 60.00; a limit there sits under the market.
wrong.Hold it to the close: Waiting hands back what the open gave you.
wrong.Hold it to 10R: The second third comes off at 5R, and the price is already past it.

questions.q: On a news gapper the stop moves to breakeven at the first trim by default.
questions.answer: True
questions.why: True. The stop moves to breakeven between 2R and 5R, and by default at the first trim.
questions.lesson_line: First trim, then the stop to breakeven.

questions.q: Buy, or wait for the pullback?
questions.story: The stock gapped 9% on a report. At 9:50 it trades over the 5-minute high, still above its open, with the day's average volume already traded. The day's low is 2% under the price.
choices: Buy at market; stop under the day's low
Wait; the pullback is the only entry
Buy half now, half at the close
Buy at tomorrow's open
questions.answer: Buy at market; stop under the day's low
questions.why: Buy at market. By our current default, day one over the opening-range high is the A+ form, and the pullback is the other way in. The stop goes a few cents under the day's low, 2% away.
questions.lesson_line: Day one over the opening-range high is the A+ form.

wrong.Wait; the pullback is the only entry: By our current default we teach both. Day one over the opening-range high is the A+ form; the pullback is the other way in.
wrong.Buy half now, half at the close: Half now and half later is two prices, not one buy.
wrong.Buy at tomorrow's open: Waiting for tomorrow's open gives up the trigger.

questions.q: Which lesson owns the day, and which the pullback buy?
questions.story: The gap day is a report's reaction day on an established leader clearing a four-month base.
choices: PEG owns the day; we teach the buy
This lesson owns both
Gap Support owns the first pullback
The Episodic Pivot owns the gap day
questions.answer: PEG owns the day; we teach the buy
questions.why: The PEG owns the day; the pullback buy is taught here. A report's reaction day on an established leader clearing its base is the PEG. The first-pullback entry on either is taught here.
questions.lesson_line: A report day on a leader is a PEG. The pullback entry is taught here.

wrong.This lesson owns both: The PEG lesson owns a report reaction day on a leader.
wrong.Gap Support owns the first pullback: Gap Support is the later test of the gap-up low, not the first pullback.
wrong.The Episodic Pivot owns the gap day: An Episodic Pivot is a neglected name, not a leader clearing a base.

questions.q: News Gapper or News Failure?
questions.story: A contract headline gaps a stock up 8% at the open. By the close it is 2% under the prior close.
choices: A News Failure; the opposite trade
A News Gapper; the headline was good
A News Gapper; buy the pullback
A Kicker; the close was weak
questions.answer: A News Failure; the opposite trade
questions.why: A News Failure. A gapper holds its gap and closes green in the upper half. A gap on good news that closes under the prior close is a News Failure: same headline, opposite trade.
questions.lesson_line: Same headline, red close: the opposite trade.

wrong.A News Gapper; the headline was good: Good news does not make a gap hold. The close decides.
wrong.A News Gapper; buy the pullback: A close under the prior close is not a gap that held.
wrong.A Kicker; the close was weak: A Kicker needs a weak red close the day before the gap.

questions.q: News Gapper or Kicker?
questions.story: Monday ends with a weak red close. Tuesday opens 2% higher on 1.6x volume with no headline.
choices: A Kicker; weak red close, small gap
A News Gapper; any gap counts
A PEG; the stock gapped up
An Episodic Pivot; the close was weak
questions.answer: A Kicker; weak red close, small gap
questions.why: A Kicker. It needs a weak red close and then a small gap on positioning, rarely a headline. A News Gapper has a named catalyst and at least 3 times volume.
questions.lesson_line: A weak red close and a small gap with no news is a Kicker.

wrong.A News Gapper; any gap counts: A News Gapper needs a named catalyst and at least 3 times volume.
wrong.A PEG; the stock gapped up: A PEG is a report's reaction day, and there was none.
wrong.An Episodic Pivot; the close was weak: An Episodic Pivot needs a named surprise on a neglected name.

questions.q: News Gapper or Gap Support?
questions.story: Five weeks after a report gap, the stock dips to the gap-up low, undercuts it slightly, and closes back over it.
choices: Gap Support, the later test
A News Gapper pullback buy
A News Failure; the gap broke
A PEG; it is an earnings stock
questions.answer: Gap Support, the later test
questions.why: Gap Support. The gapper's pullback stays above the gap-day low and reclaims within about ten sessions. Gap Support is the later test of the gap-up low itself, bought as that low is defended.
questions.lesson_line: A test of the gap-up low weeks later is Gap Support.

wrong.A News Gapper pullback buy: The News Gapper pullback comes within about ten sessions and stays above the gap-day low.
wrong.A News Failure; the gap broke: A News Failure is a red close on day one, not a test weeks later.
wrong.A PEG; it is an earnings stock: A PEG is the report's reaction day, not a test five weeks on.

questions.q: News Gapper or Episodic Pivot?
questions.story: A stock nobody follows has been flat for six months. A contract headline gaps it 18% on 9x volume, the first gap in a year.
choices: An Episodic Pivot; a neglected name
A News Gapper; any headline gap is one
A PEG; it gapped on volume
A Kicker; the stock was quiet
questions.answer: An Episodic Pivot; a neglected name
questions.why: An Episodic Pivot. An EP is the first big gap in six months on a neglected name. A gapper can come from a stock that was not neglected.
questions.lesson_line: A first gap in six months on a forgotten name is an EP.

wrong.A News Gapper; any headline gap is one: The six months before the gap and the first gap in a year make it an EP.
wrong.A PEG; it gapped on volume: A PEG is a report reaction day on an established leader.
wrong.A Kicker; the stock was quiet: A Kicker needs a weak red close and a small gap on positioning.

questions.q: Grade each as a Buy 2.
questions.story: Two 11% gaps on record volume. One is on a stock flat for three months. The other is on a stock up 42% in three months.
choices: First stronger; second a B-
Both A+; both have record volume
Second stronger; it has momentum
Both B-; 11% is small
questions.answer: First stronger; second a B-
questions.why: First stronger, second a B-. Quiet before the gap is an A+ cue. Up 30% or more already is a B- cue.
questions.lesson_line: Quiet before the gap is an A+ cue. A late gap is a B-.

wrong.Both A+; both have record volume: Record volume is the same, but the months before the gap differ.
wrong.Second stronger; it has momentum: A big run into the gap is the late-gap warning, not a plus.
wrong.Both B-; 11% is small: A gap of 10% or more is an A+ cue, not a small one.

questions.q: Grade each close.
questions.story: Same gap, same volume, two stocks. One closes at 93% of its range. The other closes at 60% of its range.
choices: First an A+ cue; second a plain gapper
Both the same; the gap decides
First a B-; too close to the high
Both A+; both closed green
questions.answer: First an A+ cue; second a plain gapper
questions.why: First an A+ cue, second a plain gapper. A close in the top quarter of the range is an A+ cue. A close in the upper half holds the gap but earns no extra.
questions.lesson_line: Top-quarter close is an A+ cue. Upper half just holds the gap.

wrong.Both the same; the gap decides: The close is half the story, and these two differ.
wrong.First a B-; too close to the high: A close near the high is the best close, not a flaw.
wrong.Both A+; both closed green: Only a top-quarter close is the A+ cue; 60% is not.

questions.q: Grade the catalyst of each.
questions.story: Two stocks gap 12% on 4x volume. One gaps on a government contract. The other gaps on an analyst upgrade.
choices: Contract stronger; an upgrade is a B-
Both A+; the gap and volume match
Upgrade stronger; analysts move stocks
Same grade; a gap is a gap
questions.answer: Contract stronger; an upgrade is a B-
questions.why: The contract is stronger; an upgrade is a B- catalyst. A business-changing deal is an A+ catalyst. Bonde: upgrades have a low probability of follow-through.
questions.lesson_line: A business-changing deal beats an analyst upgrade.

wrong.Both A+; the gap and volume match: The catalyst is what differs, and it is part of the grade.
wrong.Upgrade stronger; analysts move stocks: An upgrade alone has a low probability of follow-through.
wrong.Same grade; a gap is a gap: Both gaps have the same size; the catalyst decides the grade.

questions.q: Account 40,000. Risk 0.5%. Fill 105.11, stop 103.20. How many shares?
questions.why: 104. Account times risk percent, divided by the fill minus the stop, rounded down. The stop sets the size.
questions.lesson_line: Stop first, distance second, size last.

questions.q: Buy the reclaim?
questions.story: A news gap on Monday, a clean pullback, and a reclaim that triggers on Thursday. The company reports Friday after the close.
choices: No; a report is within 3 sessions
Yes; the reclaim is perfect
Yes, at half size
Yes, and hold it through the report
questions.answer: No; a report is within 3 sessions
questions.why: No. A news gapper with a report due within 3 sessions waits. We take no new buys in the 3 days before a report.
questions.lesson_line: With a report in the next 3 sessions, no new buy.

wrong.Yes; the reclaim is perfect: A perfect chart does not remove the report risk.
wrong.Yes, at half size: Half size is still a new buy in the report window.
wrong.Yes, and hold it through the report: Holding through a report needs 5R, not a new position.

questions.q: What now?
questions.story: Seven sessions after the gap, the stock closes under the gap-day low. You have not bought yet.
choices: Off; no Buy 2
Keep waiting for a deeper pullback
Buy at the close; it is cheap
On; only a gap fill ends it
questions.answer: Off; no Buy 2
questions.why: Off. A close under the gap-day low in the first ten sessions invalidates the setup. There is nothing to buy.
questions.lesson_line: A close under the gap-day low ends it.

wrong.Keep waiting for a deeper pullback: The gap-day low gave way on a close. Waiting does not undo that.
wrong.Buy at the close; it is cheap: Buying cheaper is not the test; the line has to hold.
wrong.On; only a gap fill ends it: A close under the gap-day low also ends it.

questions.q: Where does the stop go?
questions.story: A friend quotes Morales and Kacher and says to allow a little room: put the stop 2% under the pullback low.
choices: A few cents under the pullback low
2% under the pullback low
Under the gap-day low
At the prior close
questions.answer: A few cents under the pullback low
questions.why: A few cents under the pullback low. No porosity: Morales and Kacher allow a 1 to 2% undercut. Here the stop is the exit and it only moves up.
questions.lesson_line: No porosity. The stop is the exit.

wrong.2% under the pullback low: That is porosity. Our stop is a few cents under a real low.
wrong.Under the gap-day low: The gap-day low is the line to hold, not our stop.
wrong.At the prior close: The prior close is far too wide for a stop.

questions.q: Coming out of a correction, the recent earnings gappers often lead on the other side.
questions.answer: True
questions.why: True. Coming out of corrections it is the recent earnings gappers that often have stellar performance on the other side.
questions.lesson_line: After a correction, watch the recent earnings gappers.

questions.q: Take the reclaim?
questions.story: An $8 stock that trades about $6 million a day gaps 20% on a contract. It holds the gap and sets up a clean pullback.
choices: No; under $10 and $20 million a day
Yes; the gap day's volume is huge
Yes, at half size
Yes; an $8 stock is cheap to size
questions.answer: No; under $10 and $20 million a day
questions.why: No. The stock is under $10 and trades under $20 million a day. A great gap does not change the liquidity rule.
questions.lesson_line: Ten dollars and twenty million a day, or we skip.

wrong.Yes; the gap day's volume is huge: The rule is about the usual dollar volume, not one big day.
wrong.Yes, at half size: Half size does not fix a liquidity failure.
wrong.Yes; an $8 stock is cheap to size: Both the price and the dollar volume fail.

questions.q: Fill 33.55, stop 32.59. How far is the stop from the fill, in percent?
questions.why: 2.9. The fill minus the stop, divided by the fill. That sits inside the usual 3%.
questions.lesson_line: Stop distance is the fill minus the stop, over the fill.

questions.q: Hold or sell?
questions.story: You are up 4R on a news gapper and took the first third at 3R. The next report is tomorrow after the close.
choices: Sell before the report; not up 5R
Hold; the news was a winner last time
Hold half, sell half
Hold; the stop protects you
questions.answer: Sell before the report; not up 5R
questions.why: Sell before the report. Hold through the next report only if up 5R. Up 4R is not enough.
questions.lesson_line: Under 5R going into a report, sell first.

wrong.Hold; the news was a winner last time: The last news says nothing about the next report.
wrong.Hold half, sell half: Half a position under 5R still carries the report risk.
wrong.Hold; the stop protects you: A stop does not protect against a gap through it.

questions.q: What was that loss?
questions.story: AVAV, 2024. A 15.3% gap on 15.8x volume closed at 79% of its range. You bought the 8-session pullback and reclaim at 162.59. It went straight to the stop at 158.43.
choices: A planned loss on a late reclaim
A mistake; the gap was too big
A mistake; the volume was too high
A broken rule; the stop was too tight
questions.answer: A planned loss on a late reclaim
questions.why: A planned loss on a late reclaim. A big-volume gap does not protect a late Buy 2, and the stop did its job.
questions.lesson_line: A big-volume gap does not protect a late pullback buy.

wrong.A mistake; the gap was too big: A big gap on huge volume is a plus, not a flaw.
wrong.A mistake; the volume was too high: Heavy volume is part of the setup.
wrong.A broken rule; the stop was too tight: The stop sat under the pullback low as the rules say.

questions.q: Where does the pullback buy fail most often?
choices: Early reclaim after a wide day-one bar
A reclaim after a quiet 4-day pullback
A reclaim on a clean inside day
A reclaim that holds the upper half
questions.answer: Early reclaim after a wide day-one bar
questions.why: An early reclaim after a very wide day-one bar. Three of the four losing reclaims came on day 4, the earliest after a two-session pullback.
questions.lesson_line: Beware the early reclaim after a very wide first day.

wrong.A reclaim after a quiet 4-day pullback: A quiet pullback that holds the low is the good version.
wrong.A reclaim on a clean inside day: An inside day that holds the gap-day low is a good pullback.
wrong.A reclaim that holds the upper half: Holding the upper half of the gap day is an A+ cue.

questions.q: What does the plan do on day ten?
questions.story: PEN, 2026. An 11.1% gap on 18.2x volume, in a stock already up 23.8% over 65 sessions. You bought the day-4 reclaim at 357.70, and it has drifted under 1R since.
choices: Sells it; under 1R at ten sessions
Holds it; the stop has not been hit
Adds to it; it is coiling
Moves the stop to the gap-day low
questions.answer: Sells it; under 1R at ten sessions
questions.why: It sells the trade. Time stop: under 1R after 10 sessions, sell. The reclaim reached only 0.45R and drifted for ten sessions before the stop.
questions.lesson_line: Under 1R after ten sessions, the trade is sold.

wrong.Holds it; the stop has not been hit: The time stop exists for exactly this trade.
wrong.Adds to it; it is coiling: Adding breaks one buy, one price, one stop.
wrong.Moves the stop to the gap-day low: The stop only moves up, never to the gap-day low.

questions.q: Is it an earnings gapper?
questions.story: GE, 2015. A 5.4% gap on 10.0x volume closes at 90% of its range. The earnings calendar shows no report that day.
choices: Not earnings; find the headline first
An earnings gapper; volume says so
An earnings gapper; the close says so
No setup; it was not earnings
questions.answer: Not earnings; find the headline first
questions.why: Not earnings. The calendar shows no report that day, so this is a news gap and you need the headline. Calling every big gap earnings without checking is a mistake: a quarter are not.
questions.lesson_line: Check the calendar. A quarter of big gaps are not earnings.

wrong.An earnings gapper; volume says so: Volume does not tell you the catalyst. The calendar does.
wrong.An earnings gapper; the close says so: A strong close shows strength, not the catalyst. The calendar does.
wrong.No setup; it was not earnings: A gap with no report is not thrown out. It needs a named headline.

questions.q: Is it a News Gapper?
questions.story: AAPL, 2022. The report was the day before. The stock gaps up 4.1% on 1.7x its 50-day volume and closes at its high.
choices: No; volume is under 3 times
Yes; it closed at the high
Yes; earnings gaps need less volume
No; the gap was too small
questions.answer: No; volume is under 3 times
questions.why: No. The volume was 1.7x the 50-day average, under the line of at least 3 times. The close at the high does not fix thin volume.
questions.lesson_line: Under three times average volume is not a News Gapper.

wrong.Yes; it closed at the high: A strong close does not replace the volume line.
wrong.Yes; earnings gaps need less volume: The line is at least 3 times, earnings or not.
wrong.No; the gap was too small: Volume is the failing test here, not the size of the gap.

questions.q: Is it a News Failure?
questions.story: NFLX, 2018. A 9.2% gap on 3.3x volume. The low of the day is 35.65, above the prior close of 34.64, and it closes at 35% of its range.
choices: No; it closed green and held the gap
Yes; any fade is a failure
Yes; it closed in the lower half
Yes; the high was never held
questions.answer: No; it closed green and held the gap
questions.why: No. The gap held, since the low stayed above the prior close of 34.64. The day closed green, so it is not a News Failure. It is a weak, faded close, not a red one.
questions.lesson_line: A fade that closes green is weak, not a News Failure.

wrong.Yes; any fade is a failure: A News Failure closes red or trades back to the prior close.
wrong.Yes; it closed in the lower half: A weak close is not the failure. A red close or a filled gap is.
wrong.Yes; the high was never held: Not holding the high is a fade, not a failure.

questions.q: How does it grade?
questions.story: URI, 2024. A gap on earnings on 4.0x volume, close at 89% of its range, on a stock up 42% over the prior 65 sessions.
choices: Late in a run; a B- at best
A+; 4.0x volume and a high close
Fine; the close is near the high
A+; strength begets strength
questions.answer: Late in a run; a B- at best
questions.why: Late in a run, a B- at best. The stock was up 42% in the prior 65 sessions, past the line of about 30%. A late gap carries the climax risk.
questions.lesson_line: A gap on a stock already up 42% is late.

wrong.A+; 4.0x volume and a high close: Volume and the close are good; the run into the gap is the problem.
wrong.Fine; the close is near the high: A strong day does not erase a 42% run into it.
wrong.A+; strength begets strength: A big run into the gap is the late-gap warning, not a plus.

questions.q: Write the plan: entry, stop, first trim.
questions.story: PANW, 2021. An 11.6x volume gap held its low through a 6-session pullback. On day 8 the stock trades over the prior day's high at 77.06. The stop goes at 75.92.
choices: Market 77.06; stop 75.92; third at 80.48
Limit 74.00; stop 70.00; hold
Market at close; stop 77.06; 2R
Market 77.06; no stop; third at 10R
questions.answer: Market 77.06; stop 75.92; third at 80.48
questions.why: Market 77.06, stop 75.92, a third at 80.48. One R is the fill minus the stop; three of those above the fill is 80.48. PANW reached 14.2R.
questions.lesson_line: Entry, stop and first trim, written before the open.

wrong.Limit 74.00; stop 70.00; hold: A limit far below never fills, and a stop that wide breaks the size rule.
wrong.Market at close; stop 77.06; 2R: A stop at the entry is no stop, and the first trim is 3R.
wrong.Market 77.06; no stop; third at 10R: A real stop goes in with the broker, and the first third is at 3R.

questions.q: A pullback that dips under the gap-day midpoint is graded down.
questions.answer: True
questions.why: True. A first pullback that holds the upper half of the gap day is an A+ cue. One that dips under the gap-day midpoint is a B- cue.
questions.lesson_line: Holding the upper half is A+. Under the midpoint is a B-.

questions.q: Grade each pullback.
questions.story: Two stocks gap on reports and close strong. The first one's pullback never leaves the upper half of the gap day. The second one's pullback dips under the gap-day midpoint but holds the low.
choices: First an A+ cue; second a B-
Both the same; both hold the low
First a B-; shallow means weak
Both A; any pullback is fine
questions.answer: First an A+ cue; second a B-
questions.why: First an A+ cue, second a B-. The first pullback holds the upper half of the gap day. The second dips under the gap-day midpoint.
questions.lesson_line: A shallow pullback grades above a deep one.

wrong.Both the same; both hold the low: Both hold the low, but the depth still grades.
wrong.First a B-; shallow means weak: A shallow pullback shows strength, not weakness.
wrong.Both A; any pullback is fine: The depth of the pullback is part of the grade.

questions.q: What do you do?
questions.story: A stock has gapped up two days in a row, each on wider ranges. Today a news headline gaps it a third time on 4x volume.
choices: Pass; a third gap in a burst is late
Buy day one; the volume is strong there
Buy the pullback tomorrow morning
Short it; it looks exhausted now
questions.answer: Pass; a third gap in a burst is late
questions.why: Pass. The setup is not the 3rd to 5th day of a straight-up burst. Buying the third gap of a parabolic burst is a mistake.
questions.lesson_line: The third gap of a burst is late. Pass.

wrong.Buy day one; the volume is strong there: Good volume does not fix a third gap in a burst.
wrong.Buy the pullback tomorrow morning: A pullback buy still needs a setup that is not late.
wrong.Short it; it looks exhausted now: A late gap is a reason to pass, not to short.

questions.q: How does the volume grade?
questions.story: A stock gaps on a report. By 9:50, twenty minutes after the open, it has already traded its full average daily volume.
choices: An A+ cue
A B- cue; too early to tell
No cue; only the close counts
A disqualifier; too much too fast
questions.answer: An A+ cue
questions.why: An A+ cue. The average daily volume trading in the first 15 to 20 minutes is an A+ volume cue. Kullamagi: ideally the stock trades its average daily volume the first 15 to 20 minutes or quicker.
questions.lesson_line: A day's average volume in 20 minutes is an A+ cue.

wrong.A B- cue; too early to tell: Twenty minutes is the window, and the cue is already met.
wrong.No cue; only the close counts: Volume early in the day is the point of the cue.
wrong.A disqualifier; too much too fast: Heavy early volume is the cue, not a flaw.

questions.q: May you take the reclaim?
questions.story: You have been stopped out of the same stock three times this week on three clean reclaims. A fourth reclaim triggers on Friday.
choices: No; three tries a week are used
Yes; a new trigger is a new trade
Yes, at double size
Yes, with a wider stop
questions.answer: No; three tries a week are used
questions.why: No. At most 3 tries a week and 6 in a month on one stock. After a stop-out, buy again only on a new trigger, as a new trade.
questions.lesson_line: Three tries a week on one stock, then stop.

wrong.Yes; a new trigger is a new trade: A new trigger is a new trade, but the tries per week are capped.
wrong.Yes, at double size: Doubling size to win it back breaks the sizing rule.
wrong.Yes, with a wider stop: A wider stop breaks the stop rule.

questions.q: The risk formula says 666 shares. The stock's average daily volume is 40,000 shares. How many shares may you buy?
questions.why: 400. The size is the smaller of the risk-based size and the position cap. We never own more than 1% of a stock's average daily volume.
questions.lesson_line: Size is the smaller of the risk formula and the cap.

questions.q: Hidden ticker, five sessions after a gap on a report. Did the pullback hold the gap-day low? Take the reclaim or pass.
choices: Take it; the pullback held the low
Pass; the gap-day low gave way
Pass; the gap has filled
questions.answer: Take it; the pullback held the low
questions.why: Take it. A 14.2% gap on 4.8x volume closed at 94% of its range. A 4-session pullback, 2.8% deep, held the gap-day low, then reclaimed the prior high.
questions.lesson_line: A held gap-day low and a clean reclaim is the setup.

wrong.Pass; the gap-day low gave way: No close in the pullback sat under the gap-day low.
wrong.Pass; the gap has filled: Price never traded back to the prior close.

questions.q: Hidden ticker, an earnings gap day is the last bar. Was the stock quiet or already run up before it? Take it or pass.
choices: Pass; it was already up too much
Take it; the gap day closed strong
Take it; the volume was heavy
questions.answer: Pass; it was already up too much
questions.why: Pass. The stock was up 42% over the prior 65 sessions, past the line of about 30%. A late gap in a stock already run up carries the climax risk.
questions.lesson_line: A big run into the gap is the warning. Pass.

wrong.Take it; the gap day closed strong: A strong close does not erase a big run into the gap.
wrong.Take it; the volume was heavy: Heavy volume does not make a late gap early.

questions.q: Grade this one.
questions.story: Report beats with a raise. A 12% true gap on the highest volume in a year, closing in the top quarter. It comes out of a 4-month quiet range above a rising 200-day. Green market.
choices: A+; the cues line up
B-; a pullback is not day one
No trade; it needs an earnings date
A; a gap is only A+ at 15%
questions.answer: A+; the cues line up
questions.why: A+. A beat and a raise, a true gap of 10% or more and the year's top volume all line up. So do a top-quarter close and a quiet range above a rising 200-day.
questions.lesson_line: When every cue lines up, size up. That is an A+.

wrong.B-; a pullback is not day one: The grade is about the cues, not whether you buy day one or the pullback.
wrong.No trade; it needs an earnings date: The report is the catalyst; it already has a date.
wrong.A; a gap is only A+ at 15%: The A+ gap cue is 10% or more.

questions.q: Day-one buys and pullback buys share the same trims, trail, breakeven and time stop.
questions.answer: True
questions.why: True. A third at 3R, a third at 5R, the stop to breakeven at the first trim, the trail under the 10- or 21-day, and the time stop under 1R after 10 sessions apply to both.
questions.lesson_line: The exit plan is the same for both ways in.

questions.q: What is the lesson?
questions.story: SEDG, 2019. A 15.0% gap on 11.4x volume. You bought the day-4 reclaim at 51.76, with the stop under the pullback low. It failed the next session.
choices: A planned loss; the stop worked
The gap was too big to be trusted
You should have bought the open
The stop should have been wider
questions.answer: A planned loss; the stop worked
questions.why: A planned loss; the stop worked. The day-4 reclaim failed the next session and the whole gap was given back within weeks. The stop kept the loss small.
questions.lesson_line: A reclaim that fails costs the stop and no more.

wrong.The gap was too big to be trusted: Size is not the flaw; a failed reclaim is part of the plan.
wrong.You should have bought the open: We do not buy the open before the range forms.
wrong.The stop should have been wider: The stop only moves up; widening it turns a small loss into a big one.

questions.q: What keeps the plan alive?
questions.story: In our scan of news gappers, roughly three in ten reach 3R before the stop. The rest do not.
choices: Small stops and trims at 3R and 5R
A wider stop that rarely gets hit
Adding more when volume climbs fast
Skipping every pullback buy
questions.answer: Small stops and trims at 3R and 5R
questions.why: Small stops and trims at 3R and 5R. In our scan about three in ten reached 3R before the stop, so most buys never get there. The stop sets the size, so each loss is small, and the winners are trimmed.
questions.lesson_line: Most buys never reach 3R. Small losses and trims pay for them.

wrong.A wider stop that rarely gets hit: A wider stop turns a small loss into a big one.
wrong.Adding more when volume climbs fast: One buy, one price, one stop: no adding.
wrong.Skipping every pullback buy: The pullback buy is part of the plan, not the problem.

questions.q: In the 60 sessions before a gap, the high was 58.00 and the low was 46.00. How far is the high above the low, in percent?
questions.why: 26.1%. That is under the 35% line, so the 60 sessions were a quiet range, the setting our card prefers.
questions.lesson_line: Quiet means the 60-session high is within 35% of the low.

questions.q: Which gap has the better setting?
choices: The flat base; it was quiet first
The swinger; it already has momentum
Equal; only the catalyst matters here
questions.answer: The flat base; it was quiet first
questions.why: The flat base. On our card a gap out of a base or a quiet range is preferred. The 20.00 to 31.00 swing is wider than the 35% line.
questions.lesson_line: Prefer a gap out of a base or a quiet range.

wrong.The swinger; it already has momentum: Our card prefers a quiet range first. A wide swing is not quiet.
wrong.Equal; only the catalyst matters here: The catalyst comes first, but the setting still moves the grade.

questions.story: Two stocks gap 12% on the same kind of news. One opens above a flat 5-month base. The other has swung between 20.00 and 31.00 over the last 60 sessions.

questions.q: How many shares may you own?
choices: 3,000; 1% of the average volume
20,000, since today is heavy volume
60,000, 1% of today's volume
questions.answer: 3,000; 1% of the average volume
questions.why: 3,000. The cap is 1% of average daily volume, not of today's surge. That is under the 20,000 from the stop math.
questions.lesson_line: Cap the size at 1% of average daily volume.

wrong.20,000, since today is heavy volume: A one-day surge does not lift the cap. It uses the average.
wrong.60,000, 1% of today's volume: The cap is 1% of the average daily volume, not of today's.

questions.story: A news gapper averages 300,000 shares a day but trades 6 million today. Your stop math says 20,000 shares.

questions.q: We never own more than 1% of a stock's average daily volume.
questions.answer: True
questions.why: True. Our size cap is 1% of average daily volume, and illiquid stocks are not even watched.
questions.lesson_line: One percent of average volume is the most we own.

questions.q: You bought at 80.00 with the stop at 77.00. A gap-down day's first 30-minute low is 71.00. What is the loss, in R?
questions.why: 3R. That is past the 2R ceiling, so you get out.
questions.lesson_line: First 30 minutes past 2R: get out.

questions.q: What do you do?
choices: Make 75.50 the stop and stay in
Sell at once; news gappers gap again
Drop the stop to 74.00 to give it room
questions.answer: Make 75.50 the stop and stay in
questions.why: Make 75.50 the stop and stay in. The first 30 minutes decide, and the loss at that low is under the 2R ceiling.
questions.lesson_line: News stocks gap again. The first 30 minutes decide.

wrong.Sell at once; news gappers gap again: You get out only if the first 30 minutes take the loss past 2R. Here they do not.
wrong.Drop the stop to 74.00 to give it room: The stop moves only by the gap rule: the first 30-minute low, 75.50, not a level picked for room.

questions.story: You bought at 80.00 with the stop at 77.00. Follow-up news gaps the stock open at 75.80. The first 30-minute low is 75.50, a loss of 1.5R.
